results.summary: This design is a serial balanced-ternary integer multiplier that takes two 8-bit signed operands and produces a 16-bit signed product. Internally it converts the binary operands to balanced ternary, multiplies them with a serial ternary shift-and-add core, and converts the product back to binary. It is implemented in Amaranth and uses a bit-serial protocol with strobes for loading operands, starting the multiply, and reading the result. A cocotb test exercises the protocol and corner cases, and no external hardware is required.

results.summary: This design implements a DVD-style bouncing logo on a VGA monitor, using a 128x40 bitmap that displays UACJ IIT. It includes a VGA sync generator, bouncing logic with position registers, a bitmap ROM for the logo, a color palette, an RGB output multiplexer with scanline and glitch effects, and a VHS-style corruption engine. The design is written in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout ASIC shuttle. It uses the Tiny VGA pinout for video output and needs no external hardware beyond a VGA display.
